title: Fix: deduplicate unparsed -webkit-mask declarations
author: franciscolourenco
summary: When an authored `-webkit-mask`/`mask` pair has an unparsed value (e.g. var()), prefixing duplicates `-webkit-mask`; the PR merges an unparsed declaration into the previous one when it is the same property with identical tokens, in the mask handler and in @supports color fallbacks. The bug is real but harmless (identical duplicate). The fix only covers mask, though the same bug is in transition/animation/transform/border-radius handlers.
evidence: master 574eee2 CLI with --targets 'chrome 90': `.foo{-webkit-mask:url(m.svg) var(--o);mask:url(m.svg) var(--o)}` -> `-webkit-mask` emitted twice, then `mask`. Still reproduces. No reviews. Design question for review (calibration #1416): the helper is applied per handler; a shared place (e.g. where unparsed prefixed properties are pushed) may be preferred so the other handlers get it too.
